subject: Geography

source.title: National curriculum in England: geography programmes of study

coverage.yearStructure: key-stage programme; no statutory year-by-year sequence
coverage.ks4: not applicable as a national curriculum programme

statementPolicy: Controlled paraphrases only. Example content in square brackets is not represented as statutory objectives.

KS1.summary: Name and locate the world's seven continents and five oceans.
Name and locate the four countries and capital cities of the United Kingdom and its surrounding seas.
Compare human and physical geography of a small area of the United Kingdom with a contrasting non-European area.
Identify seasonal and daily weather patterns in the United Kingdom and locate hot and cold areas in relation to the Equator and the poles.
Use basic vocabulary for key physical features such as coasts, forests, hills, mountains, rivers, soil and vegetation.
Use basic vocabulary for key human features such as cities, towns, villages, farms, factories, ports, harbours and shops.
Use world maps, atlases and globes to identify the United Kingdom, countries, continents and oceans studied.
Use simple compass directions and locational language to describe locations and routes on maps.
Use aerial photographs and plan perspectives to recognise features, devise simple maps and use basic symbols and keys.
Use simple fieldwork and observation to study the school, its grounds and the surrounding environment.

KS2.summary: Locate countries using maps, with focus on Europe, North America and South America and their environmental regions and major human and physical characteristics.
Name and locate UK counties, cities and geographical regions and describe identifying human and physical characteristics, topographical features and land-use patterns.
Understand the position and significance of latitude, longitude, the Equator, hemispheres, the Tropics, polar circles, the Prime Meridian and time zones.
Compare human and physical geography of a UK region, a region in a European country and a region in North or South America.
Describe and understand physical geography including climate zones, biomes, vegetation belts, rivers, mountains, volcanoes, earthquakes and the water cycle.
Describe and understand human geography including settlement, land use, economic activity, trade links and natural resource distribution.
Use maps, atlases, globes and digital mapping to locate countries and describe studied features.
Use compass points, grid references, symbols and keys, including Ordnance Survey maps, to develop knowledge of the United Kingdom and wider world.
Use fieldwork to observe, measure, record and present local human and physical features through maps, plans, graphs and digital technologies.

KS3.summary: Extend locational knowledge and spatial awareness of world countries, with focus on Africa, Russia, Asia and the Middle East and their environmental regions and major human and physical characteristics.
Understand geographical similarities, differences and links through study of a region in Africa and a region in Asia.
Understand physical geography processes including plate tectonics, rocks, weathering, soils, weather and climate change, glaciation, hydrology and coasts.
Understand human geography processes including population, urbanisation, international development, economic sectors and natural resource use.
Understand how human and physical processes interact to change landscapes, environments and climate and how human activity depends on natural systems.
Develop routine use of globes, maps and atlases in classroom and field contexts.
Interpret Ordnance Survey maps using grid references, scale, topographical and thematic mapping, and aerial and satellite photographs.
Use Geographical Information Systems to view, analyse and interpret places and data.
Use fieldwork in contrasting locations to collect, analyse and draw conclusions from geographical data using increasingly complex information sources.
